seo_title: Sperm Whale Dives Exceed 2,000 Meters in Search of Giant Squid
fact_hook: This whale hunts deeper than many submarines can travel.
fact_explanation: Sperm whales are capable of diving beyond 2,000 meters and remaining submerged for over an hour while hunting deep-sea squid, including large species such as the colossal squid.
impact_paragraph_1: At these depths, pressure surpasses 200 atmospheres, yet sperm whales tolerate it through collapsible lungs and oxygen-rich muscles that store vast reserves of myoglobin.
impact_paragraph_2: Their abyssal hunting expeditions link surface ecosystems to deep-ocean food webs, demonstrating how the largest toothed predators on Earth routinely operate in zones once considered biologically inaccessible to mammals.
did_you_know: Sperm whales produce some of the loudest biological sounds on the planet to echolocate in darkness.
subject: Sperm Whale
